physics-killer-01.material: For roller coaster rail wey no get friction, object start from rest for point A wey get height $50\,\mathrm{m}$. Di heights of three points for di rail dey for di table. Point B: $45\,\mathrm{m}$, point C: $30\,\mathrm{m}$, point D: $5\,\mathrm{m}$. Ignore air resistance and take $g=10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$. Which one correctly match, in order, how many times di speed for C na di speed for B, and di speed for D?
physics-killer-01.thinking.0: Work and conversion between mechanical energies
physics-killer-01.s.s1.prompt: For roller coaster rail wey no get friction, object start from rest for point A wey get height $50\,\mathrm{m}$. Di heights of three points for di rail dey for di table. Point B: $45\,\mathrm{m}$, point C: $30\,\mathrm{m}$, point D: $5\,\mathrm{m}$. Ignore air resistance and take $g=10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$. Which one correctly match, in order, how many times di speed for C na di speed for B, and di speed for D?
physics-killer-01.s.s1.explain: Because e dey rest for A, from $mgh_A=\frac12mv^2+mgh$ to $v=\sqrt{2g(h_A-h)}$. $v_B=\sqrt{2\cdot10\cdot5}=10$, $v_C=\sqrt{2\cdot10\cdot20}=20$, $v_D=\sqrt{2\cdot10\cdot45}=30\,\mathrm{m/s}$. So $v_C/v_B=2$ times, $v_D=30\,\mathrm{m/s}$. Speed no dey proportional to di height wey e fall but to $\sqrt{\Delta h}$ (wrong answer ①), if you mistake di height $5\,\mathrm{m}$ of D as di height wey e fall, e go be $10\,\mathrm{m/s}$ (wrong answer ③), and if you forget $\frac12$ e go be $\sqrt{10\cdot45}\approx21\,\mathrm{m/s}$ (wrong answer ④).

physics-killer-01.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.
